subsystems.name: Orthogonal genetic chemistry
subsystems.role: a second, chemically distinct information system that can carry heredity alongside or instead of DNA.
parts: unnatural base pairs forming a six- or seven-letter alphabet
polymerases engineered to copy and transcribe them

subsystems.name: Translation machinery
subsystems.role: reads the new alphabet and turns it into proteins containing building blocks Earth life does not use.

subsystems.name: Chassis organism
subsystems.role: the cell that hosts the new chemistry — usually a stripped-down bacterium or yeast.
parts: extremophile chassis for heat, salt, radiation or pressure

subsystems.name: Xenometabolism
subsystems.role: lets the organism eat substrates ordinary microbes cannot, so it occupies a niche nothing else competes for.

subsystems.name: Containment and biocontrol
subsystems.role: keeps a novel organism from surviving outside the bioreactor.

subsystems.name: Design and test loop
subsystems.role: builds and screens designs thousands of times faster than manual cloning.

buildSteps.title: Choose the orthogonal chemistry
buildSteps.detail: Pick a backbone, base pair or amino acid that natural enzymes ignore, and design a matching polymerase and codon assignment so the new system does not cross-talk with the cell's own DNA.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise the genome
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the sequence chemically in fragments, stitch them in yeast or in a test tube, and install the orthogonal replication and translation genes as a separate module.

buildSteps.title: Build the containment layer
buildSteps.detail: Delete or rewrite genes so the cell needs a nutrient that exists only in the lab, and add kill switches that trigger outside set conditions.

buildSteps.title: Rewire metabolism
buildSteps.detail: Insert pathways that let the organism use an unusual carbon, nitrogen or phosphorus source, and adapt its membrane and chaperones so the new chemistry works inside it.

buildSteps.title: Harden the chassis
buildSteps.detail: If the target is an extreme environment, borrow repair, membrane and protein-stability traits from organisms that already live in heat, salt, acid, radiation or high pressure.

buildSteps.title: Run directed evolution
buildSteps.detail: Grow the cells under continuous selection so the new parts co-evolve with the host; orthogonal replication can be made error-prone on purpose to speed this up.

buildSteps.title: Test escape and failure modes
buildSteps.detail: Measure how long the organism survives without its synthetic nutrient, whether it can swap genes with wild microbes, and whether the kill switch fires reliably at scale.

buildSteps.title: Scale in closed bioreactors
buildSteps.detail: Grow the strain in sealed vessels with filtered exhaust and waste treatment, then convert its products — proteins, polymers, chemicals — into useful goods.

prerequisites.why: writing a whole genome from scratch is routine in cost terms only for small genomes, and error rates still limit size.
labs have made polymerases that copy xeno nucleic acids and cells that use unnatural base pairs, but nothing yet runs a full synthetic information system at scale.
a minimal bacterial cell of roughly 470 genes has been built, and synthetic yeast chromosomes have been combined, giving a baseline for what can be removed.

prerequisites.tech: Predictive design of proteins and RNA
prerequisites.why: new polymerases, tRNAs and metabolic enzymes must be designed rather than found, and prediction is not yet reliable enough for one-shot designs.
escape-proof dependence on a lab-only nutrient has not been demonstrated over long fermentation runs in the open environment.

pathway.milestone: expanded genetic alphabets and xeno nucleic acids working inside living cells; minimal genomes built by synthesis
pathway.unlocks: proof that heredity and translation can be carried by chemistry Earth life does not share.

pathway.milestone: organisms whose core information system is fully orthogonal and which cannot exchange genes with wild microbes
pathway.unlocks: safe industrial use of biochemistry that natural competitors cannot exploit.

pathway.milestone: strains engineered or evolved to thrive in high temperature, salinity, radiation or solvent-heavy waste streams
pathway.unlocks: biomanufacturing and bioremediation where ordinary cells die.

pathway.milestone: self-contained synthetic cells that grow and divide on a designed genome
pathway.unlocks: programmable organisms for off-world or closed-loop life support — contingent on containment and biosecurity questions being settled, as recent expert assessments of mirror-image life have warned.
